118. ἐψιόωντο: instead of "they were playing." But Philoxenus [takes it] instead of "they were consorting," from the word "epos."

120. μάργος Ἔρως: by metonymy, "the one who causes madness," as also (Z 132) "of raging Dionysus" and Anacreon (fg 169 B. III 294) "melting love" and Homer "pale fear." And "laiā" is formed from "lōion," which means "better"; whence also "euōnymos" (of good name).

122. ὀκλαδόν: instead of "having crouched." LgP
123 a. 〈κατηφιόων:〉 now "being troubled, distressed." Lg
6 this gloss is wrongly ascribed to ἐπιπλομένην v. 127, transposed by W -ος -ος W : -ην -ην
b. δοιὼ δ’ ἔχεν: "astragaloi" is missing. Lg (P)
125-26. ἐπὶ προτέροισιν ὀλέ〈σσας〉: having lost these in addition to the former ones, with empty hands he lay helpless in perplexity, no longer able to defeat Eros. For Ganymede is playing with Eros.

129-30. τίπτ’ ἐπιμειδιάᾳς ἄφατον: why do you laugh, great and unspeakable evil? Either you have deceived him in vain and cheated him, and you did not overcome him justly, but you cheated him because he was inexperienced?
133. Ἀδρήστεια: Callimachus (Hymn. I 47) "Adrasteia lulled you to sleep." Sister of the Curetes.
16 sch. Call. Hymn. I 47
15 κοίμισεν (H) and Hoelzlin with Call. : -ισσεν L : -ησεν P
134. ἄντρῳ ἐν Ἰδαίῳ: either in the cave of Crete or in that of Troy; for the Trojans also claim the birth of Zeus, as Demetrius of Scepsis says (fg 53 Gaede).
17 sch. Pind. Ol. V 42 a (Theo) Strab. X 472

137-38. κύκλα: by "kykla" he means the rhombi, the circular movements. In Ionic fashion, "ta kykla" instead of "kykloi," like "lychna" and "diphra." "Hapsides" are the joints, "periēgees" are circular, running around.
20 τὰ κυκλώματα P : κύκλωμα L
140. ἑαῖς: he should have said "teais" (your). Lg (P)
141. ὁλκόν: now he means the course of the star.
143. θέλξον: instead of "release the soul." LgP
144 a. ἀμβολίη: slowness. Lg (P)
b. ἀφαυροτέρη: lesser. LgP
146. μείλια: the playthings, by which children are soothed. Homer [uses it] of gifts of hospitality (I 147 sq.): "I will give many soothing gifts."
1 sch. IV 1549 sch. A I 147 Apoll. Lex. Hom. 110, 19 B. Hesych. μείλια. μείλιον Et. M. 582, 29 Eust. 742, 56
148-50 a. ἡ δ’ ἀγανοῖσιν: the order is as follows: she, having drawn his cheeks to her, kissed him, and taking hold of him, answered with gentle words, smiling.
